ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is pale brown with a dark mid-dorsal stripe and distinct white spots on the flanks. It is identified by its translucent skin and unique bubble-nesting behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rohanixalus shyamrupus* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark-brown horizontal stripe running from its snout through the eye to the shoulder, lacking in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Rohanixalus shyamrupus* inhabits tropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters above sea level.
ai.behavior: The Hornbill Bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation surrounding its forest-stream habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rohanixalus shyamrupus* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–50 eggs in foam nests attached to leaves overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rohanixalus shyamrupus* is endemic to the Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh, India, occurring at elevations between 300 and 500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Rohanixalus shyamrupus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes, typically heard from vegetation in dense forest habitats.
